There is a third permission missing from the same identity, and it will fail the same way once the two above are consented.

Comparing the setup list in `.github/workflows/maester-action-smoke-test.md` set-wise against the actual output of `Get-MtGraphScope` (27 scopes returned, 24 documented, nothing documented that is not a default):

```
in Get-MtGraphScope but not in the list:
  AccessReview.Read.All          <- named in this issue
  DeviceManagementApps.Read.All  <- not named in this issue
  NetworkAccess.Read.All         <- named in this issue
```

`website/docs/sections/permissions.md` already lists all three, so only the workflow setup list had drifted. Since `Compare-MtGraphScope` reports every missing scope at once, `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All` would show up in the same warning if it is also unconsented on the smoke-test app registration, so it is worth granting in the same pass rather than discovering it on the next run.

#2686 fixes the documented list and adds a unit test that compares it against `Get-MtGraphScope` in both directions, so it cannot drift again silently. The test names the missing scopes and the file to edit in its failure message.

The consent itself still needs @merill, as you say. Nothing in the PR changes the tenant.

- **Still reproducible after rerunning:** [run 42497298264, attempt 2](https://github.com/maester365/maester/actions/runs/42497298264/attempts/2) has now failed on Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS. This is the existing tenant-permission issue, not a new failure introduced by #2715.
- **Earlier onset confirmed:** the same two access-review errors are already present in the [October 24 run started at 12:42 UTC](https://github.com/maester365/maester/actions/runs/40095027627/job/120875382462). - **Documentation work is complete:** #2686 merged on November 8 at 00:38 UTC. The current workflow setup guide includes all three permissions and the PR adds a scope-list drift test. As noted above, that changes documentation/tests, not tenant grants.

@merill, the remaining tenant-side action is to grant/admin-consent all **three** Graph **Application** permissions on the smoke-test identity, including `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All` noted in the previous comment. Then rerun the full workflow for fresh tokens and confirm the warning clears and the access-review checks no longer error. Please retain the existing execution-error gate.

content.text:
[maester365/maester#2560](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues/2560) can't be fixed in code. The smoke-test app in your demo tenant is missing three Graph **Application** permissions, and only you can grant and consent them. The docs part is already done: #2686 merged on Nov 8 with the corrected list and a test that stops it drifting again.

**What's missing.** The issue names two permissions, but a comment on it found a third:
- `AccessReview.Read.All`. Without it, `CIS.M365.5.3.2` and `CIS.M365.5.3.3` get a 403 Forbidden error, and that is what fails CI.
- `NetworkAccess.Read.All`
- `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All`

**Option A: Entra portal.** Go to App registrations → **DO NOT DELETE - Maester GitHub Action Smoke Test** → API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Application permissions. Add all three, then click **Grant admin consent**.

**Option B: PowerShell.** Connect to the demo tenant:

```powershell
Connect-MgGraph -TenantId <demo-tenant-id> -Scopes Application.ReadWrite.All, AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All

$sp    = Get-MgServicePrincipal -Filter "displayName eq 'DO NOT DELETE - Maester GitHub Action Smoke Test'"
$graph = Get-MgServicePrincipal -Filter "appId eq '00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000'"

foreach ($name in 'AccessReview.Read.All','NetworkAccess.Read.All','DeviceManagementApps.Read.All') {
    $role = $graph.AppRoles | Where-Object { $_.Value -eq $name -and $_.AllowedMemberTypes -contains 'Application' }
    New-MgServicePrincipalAppRoleAssignment -ServicePrincipalId $sp.Id -PrincipalId $sp.Id -ResourceId $graph.Id -AppRoleId $role.Id
}
```

Option B grants the permissions directly. They won't show under the app registration's "Configured permissions" unless you also add them there, but the tokens get them either way. If the display name doesn't match, look up the app by the `MAESTER_SMOKE_CLIENT_ID` value in the `maester-smoke-test` environment instead.

**Then check it.** Start a fresh full run so each job gets a new token:

```bash
gh workflow run maester-action-smoke-test.yaml -f run_type=full -f maester_version=preview --repo maester365/maester
```

On Ubuntu, Windows and macOS, the warning about missing permissions should be gone and both access-review checks should finish without errors. Once they do, tick the boxes and close the issue. Leave the check that fails CI on `Error` results as it is.
